quadratics.description:
Be able to answer any Quadratics question on Paper 1 without notes.

Key points:
• Complete the square and read off the vertex and line of symmetry
• Use the discriminant b² − 4ac for two, one or no real roots
• Solve quadratic inequalities with a sketch
• Solve a linear and a quadratic equation simultaneously
• Solve equations that are quadratic in a function of x, e.g. in x² or √x
• Use the discriminant for a line that is tangent to a curve

How: For each key point, rework one example from your notes or textbook, then cover the answer and do it again from memory. Write down any formula you had to look up.

First step: Open your notes on Quadratics and redo one example for the first key point without looking.

mapped.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Chemistry (9701), Paper 2 (AS Structured Questions)
units: Atomic structure: Define relative isotopic and atomic masses; Deduce electron configurations of atoms and ions
Chemical formulae and equations: Balance equations including ionic equations; Calculate empirical and molecular formulae
Moles and stoichiometry: Calculate reacting masses, moles and gas volumes; Use the mole concept with concentration and dilution
Ideal gases: Use pV = nRT to find mol, mass or Mr; Apply gas volume calculations at different conditions
Chemical bonding: Draw dot-and-cross diagrams for ionic and covalent species; Predict shapes and bond angles using electron-pair repulsion
Intermolecular forces and states: Relate structure and bonding in solids to melting point; Explain solubility and conductivity from bonding type
Enthalpy changes: Draw enthalpy cycle diagrams for Hess's law problems; Calculate enthalpy changes from average bond energies
Equilibria and Le Chatelier: Apply Le Chatelier's principle to changes in conditions; Write and use Kc expressions
Reaction rates and catalysis: Interpret rate graphs and initial rate data; Explain collisions and the Boltzmann distribution
Periodicity: Describe trends in period 3 oxides and chlorides; Explain thermal stability of carbonates and nitrates
Redox reactions and halogen chemistry: Deduce oxidation and reduction from changes in oxidation number; Describe displacement reactions of halogens and halide ions
Group 2 chemistry: Describe properties and reactions of Group 2 elements; Compare thermal stability and solubility of Group 2 compounds
Organic reactions and mechanisms: Name and draw structural isomers; Describe nucleophilic substitution and elimination
Organic preparative techniques: Choose reagents and conditions for conversions; Describe purification by distillation and recrystallisation
Isomerism and analysis: Identify structural, position and functional group isomers; Explain E–Z isomerism in alkenes
Alcohols, carbonyls and acids: Describe oxidation and esterification reactions; Test for carbonyls with 2,4-DNPH and Tollens' reagent
Practical skills in Paper 2: Plan a method and identify variables; Evaluate significant figures and errors in data
